<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing a detailed, accurate system design diagram for Agent Zero based on the provided file tree and README.

1. Project type & purpose  
   - Agent Zero is a full-stack, prompt-based “organic” AI assistant framework.  
   - It provides both a CLI interface (run_cli.py) and a rich Web UI (webui/) backed by a Python API server (python/api, run_ui.py).  
   - It’s intended to run containerized (docker/run) and integrates with external services (LLM APIs, SearxNG search, optional vector DB, TTS/STT).

2. High-level architectural layers  
   Draw the diagram in horizontal layers from top to bottom (or left to right):  
   A. Presentation Layer  
      • CLI client (run_cli.py)  
      • Web UI client (static files in webui/, index.html/css/js)  
   B. API Layer  
      • Python HTTP server (run_ui.py or run_cli.py for CLI mode)  
      • Endpoints under python/api/*.py (message, health, upload, settings, etc.)  
   C. Core Agent Engine  
      • agent.py orchestrator  
      • initialize.py, preload.py, prepare.py (startup tasks)  
      • python/extensions (message loop hooks, reflection, system-prompt injection)  
      • python/tools (built-in tool plugins: code execution, browser, knowledge, memory, etc.)  
      • python/helpers (utility modules: LLM calls, file I/O, shell helpers, search clients, vector_db, RAG, etc.)  
      • prompts/ (all system- and user-prompt templates, tool instructions)  
   D. Data & Persistence  
      • memory/ (persistent agent memory)  
      • knowledge/ (RAG knowledge bases)  
      • logs/ (chat session transcripts in HTML)  
      • example.env, settings.yaml (configuration)  
   E. External Services & Tools  
      • LLM provider APIs (OpenAI, etc.)  
      • SearxNG search engine (container mounted at docker/run/fs/etc/searxng)  
      • Optional vector DB (e.g., Chroma via python/helpers/vector_db)  
      • Browser automation (Playwright/Chromium via python/helpers/browser & lib/browser/*.js)  
      • Local shell / code execution (python/helpers/shell_local, code_execution_tool)  
      • TTS/STT (python/helpers/whisper)  
   F. Container Orchestration  
      • docker/run/docker-compose.yml  
      • Dockerfiles (Dockerfile, DockerfileKali)  
      • Mounted filesystem layout under docker/run/fs (configs, init scripts, installer scripts)

3. Component relationships & data flows  
   - User → CLI or Web UI → HTTP/WebSocket → Python API  
   - API handlers call Core Agent Engine (agent.py)  
   - Agent Engine uses:  
     * Prompt templates (prompts/)  
     * Tools (python/tools/) via helper wrappers (python/helpers/tool.py)  
     * Extensions to hook before/after message loops  
     * LLM calls for generation (python/helpers/call_llm.py)  
     * Memory & RAG: load/save context (python/helpers/memory, vector_db)  
     * File system operations (logs/, memory/, knowledge/)  
     * External search via SearxNG (python/helpers/searxng)  
     * Browser automation (lib/browser/*.js + python/helpers/browser_use)  
   - Results flow back up: Engine → API → UI or CLI → User  
   - Docker Compose wires up:  
     * Python application container  
     * SearxNG service container  
     * Optional additional services (vector DB)  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Layered architecture (Presentation → API → Business → Data → External)  
   - Plugin/module pattern for “tools” and “extensions” (easy to extend)  
   - Prompt-driven behavior: everything guided by prompt templates in prompts/  
   - Multi-agent hierarchy: parent agent spawns subordinate agents for subtasks  
   - Containerized, reproducible environment (Docker + Docker Compose)  

5. How to tailor your diagram to this project  
   - Emphasize separation of Frontend (CLI + Web UI) vs. Backend (API + Agent Engine).  
   - Highlight the Prompt subsystem (folder prompts/) feeding the Agent Engine.  
   - Show Tools as plug-in blocks that the Engine can invoke dynamically.  
   - Include the Data stores (memory/, knowledge/, logs/) as persistent volumes.  
   - Draw the Docker Compose boundary around Python, SearxNG, and any DB services.  

6. Diagram elements & styling  
   - Use clear, concise labels on each box (e.g., “Prompt Templates”, “LLM API”, “Memory Store”).  
   - Draw directional arrows for request/response and data flows (e.g., UI → API → Engine → LLM).  
   - Group related components with colored containers or shapes:  
     * Blue for Presentation  
     * Green for API & Engine  
     * Orange for Tools & Helpers  
     * Purple for Data Stores  
     * Gray for External Services  
     * Dashed border for Docker Compose environment  
   - Annotate any important ports (e.g., 50001) and service names (searxng).  

7. Detail & completeness  
   - Represent each of the top-level folders as logical components in your diagram.  
   - Call out the extension hook points (python/extensions) and tool plugins as first-class elements.  
   - Include startup scripts (initialize.py, prepare.py) as part of the Engine’s initialization block.  
   - Show how custom instruments (instruments/) plug into the tools subsystem.  
   - Capture important config files (docker-compose.yml, settings.yml, limiter.toml) within the Docker boundary.

By following this layered, component-centric approach—mapping each folder and subsystem to a box in your diagram, drawing clear arrows for interactions, and using color to distinguish layers—you will produce a system design diagram that fully represents Agent Zero’s architecture, highlights its extensibility points, and clarifies its runtime environment under Docker.
